rubric_items.reason: All nine acceptance criteria are covered by REQ-1..REQ-16, and the booking page is listed as out of scope with a reason. REQ-2 drops the link saying the window must match HMS-9's next-7-days days.
Most REQs are atomic and testable. REQ-10 repeats REQ-1's 'every Active doctor'. REQ-13 does not give the error body shape or code, so a tester cannot fully check it.
Every REQ cites the ticket. But a name-collation default ('the way the doctor list already sorts them') is listed under Out of scope while assumed is [], and the context pack does not support it.

The no-paging clash with conventions#lists is surfaced (C8) and settled by the ticket and A-02. The A-06 scope difference is disclosed with a reason. There is no silent contradiction with the intent baseline.
No questions are asked, which suits an explicit ticket. The collation and tie-break default should have been raised as an assumption or a non-blocking question, not left under Out of scope.
Plain and readable. Specialization, Department and Day schedule are missing from the glossary; this is disclosed and their meanings come from A-04.

findings.text: The tie-break collation default ('the way the doctor list already sorts them') is a real assumption, but it sits under Out of scope while assumed is []. The context pack does not document how the doctor list sorts, and same-name ties are left unspecified.

cites.quote: Default for name ties: compare doctor names the way the doctor list already sorts them.
Entries are ordered by slot start, earliest first; ties by doctor name.

findings.suggested_fix: Move the collation default into an assumed REQ (or into REQ-8/REQ-9 with status assumed) and give its basis. Add a deterministic final tie-break, such as doctor id, for doctors with the same name.

findings.text: REQ-2 leaves out the ticket's condition that the window covers the same days as the doctor page's next-7-days summary (HMS-9). That is a consistency check a tester could run.

cites.quote: the same days as the doctor page's next-7-days summary (HMS-9)
The window runs from now until the end of the 6th day after today in the hospital time zone

findings.suggested_fix: Add to REQ-2: the window covers the same days as the HMS-9 next-7-days summary.

findings.text: REQ-12 and REQ-13 give only the status codes. They do not give the JSON error shape or code, and they do not cover a malformed (non-numeric) id. Conventions use 400 for per-field ValidationError input errors.

cites.quote: message per field (`ValidationError`), unknown ids 404, conflicts 409.
An Inactive specialization returns 400 with the message `specialization is Inactive`.

findings.suggested_fix: State that errors use the standard { error: { code, message } } body, and add that a malformed id returns a 400 ValidationError, following conventions#errors.

findings.text: REQ-2, REQ-10 and the glossary meanings cite IDE answers from the cancelled run. A-01 was asked against an older ticket text (the 7th day after today), so the answer's context differs from the current ticket. No mismatch is recorded.

cites.quote: from now until the end of the 7th day after today
Reused from the cancelled run run_01M77B1NEGA2SK4TJPT0CAK6MX

findings.suggested_fix: Make the ticket lines the primary basis, and note that A-01 was given against earlier ticket wording that the current ticket now matches.

cites.quote: Hospital time zone Asia/Kolkata, currency INR.
A slot is free only inside the doctor's availability, in the future and not overlapping a Scheduled
D-0001, P-000001 and A-000001 are display codes derived from row ids; they are not stored.
message per field (`ValidationError`), unknown ids 404, conflicts 409.
Medical history appears only on the patient's own page, never in lists, the dashboard or logs.
Lists answer `{ items, page, page_size, total }`, 20 per page.
every Active doctor of the specialization and no paging
A doctor, patient, department or specialization kept for history but not offered for new use.

questions.text: How should doctor names be compared for ordering (collation, case), and what breaks a tie between two doctors with the same name (for example doctor id or code)?
